0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 23 October 1975, after the draft finalized by the Timber Stores Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 0.2 A series of Indian Standards are being formulated to cover various wooden stores largely used by Defence, Railways and other agencies. The general requirements for wooden tool handles have been already covered in IS: 620-1975*. This standard is intended to cover the requirements for wooden tent mallets including the heads and handles, which are used in pitching tents. 0.3 This standard was first published in 1964. In this revision, besides incorporating a few rnodifications in the list of species suitable for wooden tent mallets, modifications have been incorporated on tolerances on the dimensions of handle and the head of the mallet. 0.4 In the formulation of this standard, due weightage has been given to the international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevail- . ing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in this country. 0.5 For the purpose of. deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-1960t. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard covers the requirements for wooden tent mallets in three sizes, namely, large, medium and small.
� Gener,~ 1 req uircrncnts for wooden tool handles ( third revision ). tR ules for rounding off numerical values ( "pised).

2. TERMINOLOGY
2.1 For the purpose of this standard, the definitions given in IS : 620-1975� shall apply.

3. MATERIALS 3.1 Head
3.1.1 Timber 3.1.1.1 The mallet heads shall be manufactured from any of the species of timbers given in Appendix A.
3.1.1.2 The moisture content of the timber shall not exceed 18 percent. The timber shall have a slope cf grain not exceeding I in 15 and shall be free from centre heart ( pith), any kind of decay (rot), live insect attack, shakes, splits ( except hair splits) and knots ( except live pin knots). 3.1.1.3 Sound sapwood shall be permitted provided that it does not extend beyond the outer edge of the metal bands.

3.1.2 Band - Bands of large and medium heads shall be manufactured from mild steel hoop of size 25 mm X 1�6 rom and that of small heads from mild steel hoop of size 20 mm X 1�6 rnm. The bands shall be painted with red oxide paint before fixing.

3.13 Screws - Wood screw No. 8 and of 25 mm length conforming to IS : 676G-1972t shall be used for fixing the bands of the heads.
3.2 Handle - Handles shall be manu factured from any of the timber species given in the relevant Appendices to IS: 620-1975*. The requirements for tile manufactured tool handles shall be as given in IS : 620-1975*.

4. MANUfACTURE
4.1 The mallet heads and handles shall be manufactured to the shape as shown in Fig. 1 and 2 respectively.

..2 The eye in the head slall be central, accurate, smooth and of uniform taper. The edges of the ' e-hole shall be slightly chamfered. The ends of the head shall be flat . th the edges chamfered.
4.3 The bands shall be e ther lapped and brazed or' butt welded at the joint and shall be free fro n sharp edges. The holes in the bands shall be drilled clean and couns- unk just sufficiently to permit the heads of the screws fitting flush. TL.'. oands shall be closely and firmly held to-the heads with screws.

The handles shall be properly turned to the shape as shown in Fig. 2. 4.5 It is recommended that, immediately after manufacture, the handles and the heads ( before fitting of the bands) be dipped in raw linseed oil at room temperature as this treatment retards changes in moisture content. 5. DIMENSIONS AND TOLERANCES

6. WORKMANSIUP AND FINISH 6.1 The mallet heads and handles shall be properly shaped and finished smooth. The brazing or welding of the joints of the bands shall be clean.

6.2 The handles and the heads shall be interchangeable with the corresponding components of the respective mallets in the same supply.

7. TEST 7.1 Each mallet shall be struck ten times as in normal use against a block
of wood. At the end of this test, neither the head nor the handle shall show any sign of failure.

7.2 The heads or handles, when supplied separately, shall be fitted with the corresponding counterpart and tested as indicated in 7.1.

8. PRESERVATION
8.1 Unless otherwise specified by the purchaser, the heads and the randles shall be thoroughly soaked in hot ( about 900 e ) raw linseed oil for one hour and allowed to dry. They shall then be Wiped clean with a dry piece of cloth.

9. PACKING
9.1 The mallet heads and handles shall be securely tied and packed in gunny cloth in convenient lots for easy handling in transit or as specified by the purchaser.
5

D

I

2t22.U75

II. SAMPLING
10.1 The method of drawing representative samples of mallets and the criteria for conformity shall be as prescribed in Appendix B.
11. MARKING

11.1 Each head and handle shall be legibly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's name or initials or recognized trade-mark and the year of manufacture.
11.1.1 The head and handle may also be marked with the lSI Certification Mark.
NOTE - The use of the lSI Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of th e Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks) Act and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The lSI mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control whi ch is devised and supervised by lSI and operated by the producer. lSI marked produ cts are also continuously checked by lSI for conformity to that standard a. a furth er safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the lSI Certific ation Mark may be granted to manufacturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

APPENDIX B ( Clause 10.1 )
SAMPLING OF WOODEN TENT MALLETS 8-1. SAMPLING AND TESTING
B-l.1 Lot - In any consignment, all the wooden tent mallets of the same size and manufactured under similar conditions of production shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.

7

IS I 2922 - 1975
B-l.2 Visual EnmjnatlOD - All the mallets in the Jot shall be inspected for visual defects, workmanship and finish. Any mallet failing to satisfy the requirements for these characteristics shall be rejected. The mallets, which pass the visual examination, shall be subjected to further tests.

B-l.3 Selection or Samples for Farther Te.t. - The number of mallet s to be selected for further testing from those accepted as in B-l.2 shall be in accordance with col 1 and 2 of Table 1.

8-1.3.1 The samples shall be selected at random. In order to ensure the randomness of selection, the procedures given in IS : 4905-1968� maybe followed. B-l.3.2 All the mallets selected as in B-I.3 shall be tested for dimensions and tolerances, moisture content and the tests laid down under 7.

B-2. CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY
B-2.1 The lot shall be considered as conforming to the requirements of the specification if the number of mallets failing to satisfy anyone or more of the requirements does not exceed the corresponding permissible number of defectives given in col 3 of Table 1.
